title: Firehouse Sweet Potato & Beef Protein Bowls

shortDescription: Seasoned ground beef, roasted sweet potato, and cottage cheese in a high-protein bowl
subtitle: Seasoned ground beef, roasted sweet potato, and cottage cheese in a high-protein bowl
description: Roasted sweet potato cubes and seasoned ground beef share a bowl with cottage cheese, avocado, and a quick lime-herb drizzle. It is a straightforward, high-protein dinner that also reheats well for next-day lunches.

steps.title: Roast the sweet potato base
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potato cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper on two sheet pans in a single layer. Roast 25–28 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and fork-tender. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Season and brown the beef
steps.instruction: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high. Add beef and break it into crumbles, cooking 7–8 minutes until no pink remains. Drain excess fat, then stir in garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper and cook 2 more minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Build the lime-herb drizzle
steps.instruction: Whisk lime juice with olive oil, a pinch of salt, and cilantro if using. Keep it in a squeeze bottle at the cold end of the line so it stays bright instead of wilting the toppings early.

steps.title: Hold everything at the right temperature
steps.instruction: Cover beef and sweet potato in separate dishes and hold at 140°F or above until service. Keep cottage cheese, avocado, tomatoes, and green onions cold and covered until the last possible moment.

steps.title: Layer the bowls
steps.instruction: Start each bowl with roasted sweet potato, then add a portion of seasoned beef beside it rather than on top, so both stay visible and neither steams the other soft.

steps.title: Add the cottage cheese and produce
steps.instruction: Spoon cottage cheese into its own section of the bowl, then scatter avocado, cherry tomatoes, and green onions around the hot components.

steps.title: Finish and send it out
steps.instruction: Drizzle the lime-herb dressing over the top and set bowls at the pass with extra lime wedges and hot sauce on the side for anyone who wants more heat.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover seasoned ground beef and roasted sweet potato — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool seasoned ground beef and roasted sweet potato and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Cut sweet potato pieces the same size so none burn while others stay firm.
Rookie tip: Add cottage cheese cold, right before serving, so it never breaks down from residual heat.
Swap ground turkey for beef if the hall is trying to keep saturated fat lower without losing protein.
Keep hot sauce and extra lime on the side — the base recipe is intentionally mild.
tonightSpread: Main: Sweet potato and beef protein bowls
Sides: Sliced cucumber, extra lime wedges
Condiments: Hot sauce, extra cottage cheese
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool seasoned ground beef and roasted sweet potato in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Fold cold leftovers into a lunch bowl with extra greens the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It uses ingredients most halls already stock, comes together in two pans, and lands well above the crew's usual protein target without feeling like a diet plate.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: roast sweet potatoes and brown the beef up to two days ahead. Storage: keep beef, sweet potato, and cold toppings in separate containers up to 4 days; add cottage cheese and avocado at serving time. Reheating: warm beef and sweet potato together to 165°F, then top cold.
substitutions: Use ground turkey or ground bison for beef.
Use Greek yogurt if cottage cheese is unpopular.
Use roasted broccoli alongside the sweet potato for more volume.
